text: Dad, trust me! I didn't fail the test!
Leo came home from school with a worried face.
His father was waiting in the kitchen.
Leo put his schoolbag on the floor and took a deep breath.
His dad looked at him and asked, What happened?
Leo answered, I have something important to tell you.
Did you fail your math test? his father asked.
Leo quickly shook his head.
No, Dad. I did not fail the test.
Then why do you look so sad?
Leo opened his notebook and showed him the first page.
There were many red marks beside his answers.
His father became quiet for a moment.
Leo said, I knew the answers yesterday.
But this morning I was in a hurry.
I read every question too quickly.
One question asked me to choose the smallest number.
I chose the biggest number by mistake.
His dad smiled gently and sat beside him.
Making a mistake does not mean you are a failure.
It means you have found something to practise.
Leo looked at the test again.
He noticed that most of the wrong answers came from rushing.
His father gave him a simple plan.
First, read each question slowly.
Second, underline the important words.
Third, check your answer before you turn in the paper.
Leo wrote the three steps at the top of a clean page.
He practised with five short questions.
This time, he stopped and checked every answer.
He found two small mistakes and corrected them.
Leo felt better, but he was still nervous.
What if I make the same mistake tomorrow? he asked.
His dad replied, Then you will check your work again.
Learning is not about being perfect on the first try.
It is about noticing what happened and trying a better way.
The next day, Leo took another practice test.
He read the questions slowly and used his three steps.
When he finished, he checked the paper twice.
His teacher returned the test after lunch.
Leo had made one mistake, but he understood why.
His teacher wrote, Good progress. Keep checking your work.
Leo went home with a big smile.
Dad, I did not fail, he said.
I learned how to do better next time.
His father gave him a high five.
That is the most important answer of all.
Leo put the test in his notebook.
He knew that one difficult morning did not decide his future.
He could make a mistake, learn from it, and try again.
And this time, he trusted himself a little more.
